subject: Re: HelioCloud dedicated sizing request — allocation heuristics and tiebreaker
messages:
From: Andrew Chen <andrew@heliocloud.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@heliocloud.com
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask for Q4 — HelioCloud MAP v3 attached

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're finalizing our MAP for Q4 and want to lock dedicated capacity for our inference fleet. Our current estimate is ~120 A100-equivalent GPU-hours/day average with spikes to 360 for nightly batch re-encode windows. The attached MAP v3 has expected traffic curves and tentative rollout dates (ETA: Nov 15).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit that size under a Dedicated contract and what the prioritization/contention rules would be if there is simultaneous demand from other customers? Procurement also asked for a fallback plan and any penalty/credit language if we can't get burst capacity on demand.

I've attached HelioCloud-MAP-v3.pdf for reference.

—Andrew

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask for Q4 — HelioCloud MAP v3 attached

Kimberly / team,

I've reviewed the MAP. Quick summary + proposed heuristic:
- HelioCloud expected baseline = ~120 GPU-hrs/day (committed). Peaks (360) are predictable nightly batch windows, 02:00-05:00 PT.
- Existing Dedicated commitments next quarter: 3 deals with daily baselines totaling ~700 GPU-hrs/day plus 2 high-priority launches that each include small burst allowances (~80-120 hrs/day).

Heuristic proposal for contested burst windows (tie-break algorithm):
1) Protect committed baselines first (SLA-backed).
2) For burst capacity, rank by (a) contractual burst commitments (if any), (b) ARR contribution / GPU-hour, (c) customer launch criticality (go-live within 30 days), (d) historical runway (customer has multiple past overages).
3) If tie remains, apply proportional scaling by tier (e.g., two customers requesting equal burst split the available capacity pro-rata to committed baseline).

For HelioCloud specifically, I recommend: committed baseline = 120 GPU-hrs/day; granted burst entitlement = up to 200 GPU-hrs/day scheduled during 02:00-04:00 PT for the first 60 days (to start), with a firm review at T+30/T+60 to re-evaluate. Fallback: when bursts can't be served, we route non-critical batch to hosted API with reserved pool nodes and provide usage credits proportional to missed burst-hours.

Marcus — need ops feasibility and expected impact to other launch timelines. Neha — can you draft the customer-facing language for MAP/annex (fallback credits and scheduled burst windows)?

Thanks,
Karthik
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask for Q4 — HelioCloud MAP v3 attached

Team,

Operational reality: our Q4 bin-packing across regions is tight. I ran the last week's utilization against committed baselines — attaching the CSV (gpu-util-report-2026-08.csv). Key points:
- Current spare capacity in US-west dedicated pools: ~220 GPU-hrs/day nominal.
- Nightly maintenance + pre-scheduled scaling windows remove ~60 GPU-hrs/day availability during 01:30-04:30 PT on average.

Implications for Karthik's proposal: granting a 200 GPU-hrs/day burst at 02:00-04:00 PT will push the pool into preemption territory for one lower-tier customer (they currently have a small burst entitlement but no launch). Options:
A) Approve HelioCloud as proposed and proactively migrate the lower-tier customer to scheduled hosted fallback during Helio nights (needs CS coordination).
B) Split the available spare capacity pro-rata across the two customers (Helio gets ~140, other gets ~80).
C) Offer Helio a guaranteed baseline of 120 + scheduled paid reservation for additional burst capacity (on a best-effort basis) with clear credit terms if bursts fail.

I prefer option C for predictability and to avoid a hard preemption. If leadership signs off on prioritizing launches with >$X ARR or go-live within 30 days, we can choose A.

Jonas — want to flag this for revenue-impact review (we may need to reprice burst add-ons if we guarantee nightly access).

—Marcus
Director, Sales Ops
Attachment: gpu-util-report-2026-08.csv
From: Andrew Chen <andrew@heliocloud.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@heliocloud.com
Date: Tue, 01 Sep 2026 07:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask for Q4 — HelioCloud MAP v3 attached

Kimberly / Karthik — appreciate the quick review. Two ask-items from Procurement: 
1) We need a firm written commitment for baseline + scheduled burst windows in the MAP (DocuSign-able).
2) Fallback credits need to be tabled clearly: per-missed-burst-hour credit and maximum monthly credit.

HelioCloud is willing to sign premium priced burst reservations if that reduces the chance of preemption. Can you confirm whether option C above includes a per-burst SLA credit and whether Redwood will reserve the scheduled nodes ahead of time?

Thanks,
Andrew
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Andrew Chen <andrew@heliocloud.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Sep 2026 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask for Q4 — HelioCloud MAP v3 attached

Andrew — thank you. Per internal review and Ops constraints, here's the agreed allocation and commercial path forward: 

1) Allocation (short-term, Nov 15 go-live): committed baseline = 120 GPU-hrs/day reserved in US-west Dedicated pool.
2) Burst entitlement (scheduled): guaranteed scheduled reservation of an additional 100 GPU-hrs/day during 02:00-04:00 PT (first 60 days). This reservation is paid (reservation fee in MPA), and we will make a best-effort attempt to provide additional burst beyond the 100 hrs if capacity is clear.
3) Fallback & credits: if scheduled reservation cannot be served, Redwood will route non-critical batch to a reserved hosted pool and issue a credit of 1.0x price-per-GPU-hour for each missed burst-hour up to a monthly cap of 300 GPU-hours. Details will be encoded in the MAP annex and DocuSign MPA.
4) Review cadence: T+30/T+60 operational review to either expand scheduled reservation or move to a larger tranche based on actual utilization.

Next actions: Karthik/Neha — please draft the MPA annex language for the scheduled reservation and credit table. Marcus — ops to prepare the reservation provisioning plan and confirm any migration steps for the other impacted customer. Andrew — once you confirm wording we will send DocuSign (link attached).

Attaching: gpu-util-report-2026-08.csv, HelioCloud-MAP-v3.pdf
DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/link/signed/HL-8472

Thanks all — resolving this with option C to balance predictability, revenue capture, and fairness.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Account Exec — Enterprise, Redwood Inference
